intro: A router can repeatedly choose the same expert even while assigning probability to others. A load-balancing auxiliary objective combines hard assignment frequencies with average soft probabilities.
task: Return both routing statistics and their auxiliary loss. Compare a balanced batch, tied logits and a confidently collapsed router before interpreting the loss value.
requirements: router_logits is a nonempty real (N,E) matrix: one row per token and one column per expert.

Assign each token to its largest logit, breaking ties by lower expert index. Let fractions[e] be the fraction assigned to expert e, and probabilities[e] the mean stable-softmax probability for expert e.

Return a dictionary with fractions, probabilities and loss=E*sum(fractions*probabilities). The vectors have shape (E,); loss is a scalar. This is a top-one auxiliary statistic, not a capacity-limited dispatcher or a training update.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Measure two different distributions
hints.body: Hard argmax frequencies and mean softmax probabilities generally differ.

hints.title: Check the uniform-probability case
hints.body: When every soft probability is 1/E, the loss is one even if index-order ties send every token to one expert.

explanation: Balanced hard loads give loss one, but a value of one does not certify balanced routing. Uniform tied probabilities also give one while the hard assignments may all select the first expert.

Confident collapse can drive the loss toward E. One is not a universal mathematical lower bound for this finite-batch statistic, so inspect the two returned distributions instead of treating the scalar as a balance certificate.
Ported the upstream top-one load-balancing statistic to NumPy with stable softmax and deterministic index-order ties. Exposed the hard fractions and mean probabilities for direct inspection.
